name: Sarah Palin
role: Governor of Alaska (2006-2009); Republican vice-presidential nominee (2008); commentator; 2022 candidate for Alaska's House seat
summary: Populist conservative Republican who ran Alaska on ethics reform, higher oil taxes, a state-backed gas pipeline and tax cuts, and later became a Tea Party and Trump-era figure. She favors limited government, domestic oil, gas and nuclear development, gun rights, a strong military and Israel, and opposes abortion, same-sex marriage, cap-and-trade and the Affordable Care Act. She casts herself as an outsider against a political and media establishment, and in foreign policy has moved from interventionist positions in 2008 toward skepticism of new wars.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In the 2008 debate she opposed Obama's plan to mandate coverage through a universal government-run program and warned against the federal government taking over health care; in 2010 she called for market-based reform to replace the Democrats' health scheme.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: She argued for a pro-market agenda that does not pick winners and losers, and in America by Heart used Friedman's pencil example to show the damage government can do when it replaces decentralised choices; as governor she also raised oil taxes and backed a state-supported pipeline, so the answer stops at +1.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: She campaigned against Obama's plan to raise taxes on incomes above $250,000, calling tax increases job-killers and rejecting what she called redistribution of wealth, and she cut and suspended taxes as mayor and governor.

unions-good.rationale: No recorded position found; she called herself a former union member but gave no view on unions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In 2008 she demanded strict federal oversight of Wall Street and took on the oil majors in Alaska; from 2010 on she called for getting government out of the way and attacked heavy-handed environmental rules.

cut-welfare.rationale: In 2016 she criticised Republican majorities for funding programs that turn safety nets into hammocks, and in 2011 said she would cut entitlement programs and NPR and NEA funding.

legalize-drugs.rationale: She opposed legalizing marijuana in 2010 and called meth the bigger threat, but later said it was not her fight; nothing addresses recreational drugs as a whole.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: After the Snyder v. Phelps controversy she said she was not calling for any limit on free speech, and as a 2006 candidate said she opposed expanding hate-crime laws.

state-harmful.rationale: She said the government that governs least governs best and that government is too often the problem rather than the solution.

limit-guns.rationale: She is a lifetime NRA member who praised the Heller decision, joined the multi-state amicus brief for an individual right under the Second Amendment and opposed new gun laws after the Giffords shooting.

empower-police-military.rationale: She said in the 2008 debate that the country needs to grow its military, in 2010 called for a strong national defense and in 2009 opposed cuts to missile defense and the F-22; as governor she doubled police academy recruits.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: As governor she signed the omnibus crime bill HB 90, which strengthened prostitution laws.

decide-locally.rationale: In America by Heart she wrote that the Tenth Amendment means the best government is closest to the people, in 2010 she attacked federal strings on state stimulus money, and she says marriage and abortion should be left to the states.

traditional-family.rationale: In America by Heart she described the family as reciprocal with self-government, depending on family virtues, and she defined marriage as one man and one woman.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In the 2008 debate she said she did not support defining marriage as anything but one man and one woman; she has also backed DOMA and a federal amendment, and in 2012 said states should decide while she opposed it.

abortion-legal.rationale: She is pro-life with an exception only where the mother's life is at risk, named pro-life as a unifying value in 2016, and said Roe v. Wade should be overturned and left to the states.

more-religion-public.rationale: She urged leaders at the 2010 Tea Party Convention to seek divine intervention and not fear political correctness, and wrote that she fought to keep the Christmas manger and Ten Commandments displays as mayor.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In America by Heart she said Americans need to reclaim their country and heritage and honor what the country was meant to be.

reduce-immigration.rationale: She called for closing the border and deporting people in the country illegally, but that is unauthorized migration, not immigration levels.

free-trade.rationale: As governor she praised trade and exports as important to Alaska, but in 2016 she criticised lousy trade deals that gut American industry.

nation-first.rationale: In 2016 she called for a candidate who represents America first and said Washington should stop funding other nations' quarrels and fight for American interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: She backed a Darfur no-fly zone in 2008 and a Libya no-fly zone in 2011, but opposed troops for humanitarian missions in Libya and any Syria intervention in 2013.

open-borders.rationale: In 2016 she warned against a nation without borders and said borders must be secured, and in 2009 said we must close the border.

limit-growth.rationale: In her 2009 op-ed she argued energy should be abundant and affordable for American prosperity and said the country is ripe for economic growth if it taps domestic resources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2009 she called Obama's cap-and-trade plan an enormous threat to the economy and wrote that the benefits of emissions-reduction policies are far outweighed by costs.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In her convention speech she pledged to build more nuclear plants, and in 2010 she called for support for nuclear power.

experts-over-public.rationale: She repeatedly opposed Washington experts and elites and wanted common-sense solutions from ordinary people, saying all political power rests with the people.

central-planning.rationale: In America by Heart she praised the market's cooperation without central orders and in 2011 rejected the idea that government can plan the economy, retirement or security for citizens.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In her convention speech she attacked Obama's plan to raise the death tax, and in Going Rogue she urged slaying the death tax once and for all.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In 2010 she called for a pro-market agenda that does not pick winners and losers and in 2011 for eliminating all energy subsidies, though as governor she signed state seed money for the TransCanada gas pipeline.

democracy-best.rationale: In the 2008 debate she called democracy, tolerance, freedom and equal rights America's perfect ideal, and at the Tea Party Convention said democracies do not go to war with each other.

separate-church-state.rationale: She fought for religious displays like the manger and Ten Commandments and criticised an elite hostile to public faith, though she vetoed funding for private religious schools as unconstitutional.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In 2006 she said her personal beliefs would not dictate her public policies and she was not out preaching or forcing views on others, and she vetoed funding for private Christian schools as illegal.

military-superiority.rationale: She called for peace through strength and a strong national defense in 2010, said in 2008 that the military must grow, and opposed ending F-22 production and cutting missile defense.

equal-outcomes.rationale: In the 2008 debate she rejected the redistribution-of-wealth principle and in 2016 praised Trump for backing equal opportunity to work.

state-as-business.rationale: She said a governor must act as an effective CEO for Alaskans and in 2016 argued leaders should balance budgets as the private sector must.

total-state.rationale: She said that only limited government can expand prosperity and the government that governs least governs best.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: She called Israel America's strongest ally in the Middle East, backed an embassy in Jerusalem, and said in 2011 that she stood unapologetically with Israel.

school-vouchers.rationale: In her 2006 candidate profile she backed charter and home schools rather than private-school vouchers, and as governor she vetoed public funding for private religious schools as unconstitutional.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: At the 2010 Tea Party Convention she condemned the $787 billion stimulus and record deficits as generational theft and urged killing a second stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: She told the 2008 debate audience that Americans must fight for their freedoms, economic and national-security alike, and in 2010 said freedom is God-given and limited government expands prosperity.

reason-over-faith.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In 2008 she said those who are in the country legally should be first in line for services and opportunities.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: In her convention speech she said every woman can walk through every door of opportunity, and in America by Heart she called herself a conservative feminist while saying women are as able as men.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: She pushed to drill offshore and in ANWR, said drill baby drill, signed Alaska's gas pipeline act and promoted coal and domestic oil and gas in her 2009 op-ed.

national-mission.rationale: She said America must stand with people seeking freedom and spread democracy where wanted, but also said in 2016 and 2013 that America should let other countries sort out their own conflicts.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: She told Katie Couric in 2008 that women today have every opportunity a man has to succeed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: In 2016 she said the permanent political class does the bidding of its donor class; as governor she passed an ethics law and took on lobbyists and the good-old boys.

night-watchman-state.rationale: She called for limited government but as governor signed record education funding, the energy rebate and a state-supported pipeline, and talked of public safety and schools as state duties.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: She wrote in America by Heart that all human beings have a God-given right to be free and in 2008 listed equal rights among American ideals, though she opposed same-sex marriage and civil unions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: At the 2010 Tea Party Convention she said all political power is inherent in the people and government is supposed to work for them.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: At the 2010 Tea Party Convention she said competition makes people work harder and be more efficient, mainly about primaries and business.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: She said in 2008 that she had no desire to ban any book; a biographer's account of her asking a librarian about removing books in 1996 is disputed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: She backed expanding NATO to Georgia and Ukraine and said the US must work with allies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: In her convention speech she endorsed the line that small towns grow good people with honesty, sincerity and dignity and described them as the hardest-working Americans.

death-penalty.rationale: She has said she would sign a death-penalty law and described support for it for those who kill innocent people or rape and murder a child.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: She said she backed abstinence education plus contraception information that kids may not get at home, but opposed explicit programs.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: In 2006 she said schools should be allowed to teach creationism alongside evolution, then said it need not be part of the curriculum, and in 2008 said evolution should be taught and science belongs in science class.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In 2011 she said foreign assistance should go to allies who need it and appreciate it and for humanitarian purposes where it can truly help, and called borrowing to send aid to the developing world unsound.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: She backed a two-state solution in the 2008 debate but in 2011 opposed Obama's call for a state based on the 1967 lines as carving Israel in half.

precautionary-principle.rationale: She said environmental policy should weigh real-world costs and benefits rather than act on uncertain science, and sued over the polar bear listing questioning its scientific basis.

collective-defense.rationale: She told Gibson that under NATO, if another country is attacked, you are expected to be called upon and help, and backed NATO membership for Georgia and Ukraine.

ban-cartels.rationale: She said she broke the oil companies' monopoly in Alaska and insisted on competition and fairness, and in 2010 urged a pro-competition, level-playing-field agenda.

no-bailouts.rationale: In 2010 she attacked the bank, auto and other bailouts and TARP as crony capitalism, and in Going Rogue said a business must be brave enough to fail; in 2008 she had backed a congressional rescue plan.

patriotic-education.rationale: Her 2006 campaign booklet backed an ABC program of back-to-basics schooling with patriotism and ethics, and she said the Under God Pledge is good enough for her.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: She calls herself a commonsense constitutional conservative and said the Constitution is the best road map for a more perfect union.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: In Going Rogue she said an application by China's Sinopec to control Alaska gas reserves bothered her and was not in the state's or country's interest; she did not propose a general rule.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In a 2011 Fox interview she said new Social Security enrollees should be allowed personal accounts with part of the payroll tax, invested by themselves rather than planned by government.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: In the 2008 debate she described the Alaska legislature as the body that holds the purse strings and the one she worked with on budgets.

corporate-influence.rationale: She said she stood up to special interests, lobbyists and big oil as governor, refused large checks she saw as conflicts, and in 2016 said politicians do the bidding of campaign donors.

democratic-peace.rationale: At the 2010 Tea Party Convention she said America should stand with people fighting for democracy because democracies do not go to war with each other and settle disputes peacefully.

non-intervention.rationale: She backed a Darfur no-fly zone, the Iraq surge, a Libya no-fly zone and action against Iran and Iranian threats to Israel.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In the 2008 debate she pledged to ensure there would never be a second Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In the 2008 debate she said she was tolerant of adults choosing their partners and relationships and would not prohibit hospital visits or contracts.

assisted-dying.rationale: Her 2006 candidate profile reported her opposition to physician-assisted suicide.

islam-incompatible.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: At the 2010 Tea Party Convention she said all political power is inherent in the people and government works for the people, while also calling freedom God-given.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: She called for growing the military and a strong national defense.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: She wanted Georgia and Ukraine admitted to NATO against Russian pressure and called for coalitions with allies against Iran and North Korea.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: In February 2010 she said she did not think the don't-ask-don't-tell policy should be repealed right then and called the effort unnecessary.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: As governor she doubled police academy recruits, signed tougher sentencing and monitoring laws and called for strong police, court and prison funding.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: She supported the Iraq war and surge and backed pre-emptive action against imminent threats and agreed with the Bush Doctrine given sufficient intelligence.

pollution-taxes.rationale: She called Obama's cap-and-trade plan a cap-and-tax scheme that would raise electricity costs and kill jobs.

arms-reduction.rationale: She opposed New START as one-sided, wanted to grow the military and opposed cuts to missile defense and the F-22.

public-service-media.rationale: In 2011 she said she would cut federal funding for NPR and the NEA.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: She said in the 2008 debate that US nuclear weapons are a safe, stable deterrent, opposed New START as one-sided and in 2014 said only a good guy with a nuke stops a bad guy with a nuke.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: She called heavy-handed environmental laws an economic burden, and in 2009 said the country cannot afford to kill domestic energy production.

women-suffrage.rationale: She called the suffragists her feminist foremothers, said in 2008 that every woman can walk through every door of opportunity, and stood for national office herself.

no-business-privileges.rationale: She told the Tea Party Convention that government should not pick winners and losers, wrote in America by Heart that she fought crony capitalism as governor, and ended oil tax breaks in Alaska.

national-resource-control.rationale: She argued that Americans should control their own energy supply rather than outsource it to China, Russia and Saudi Arabia, and was uneasy about Sinopec controlling Alaska's gas reserves.

notes: Living person: no inference; evidence on a nearby question is left null. Views changed on foreign intervention (2008 Georgia, Iran and Darfur positions versus 2013 Syria and 2016 let-them-sort-it-out remarks) and on marriage (a federal amendment in 2008, let the states decide in 2012 while still opposing it); the recent position is used. Several quotations come through OnTheIssues compilations of her books, speeches and interviews, which were read as a reference, so those answers are at most medium unless a primary source also states them. Books Going Rogue and America by Heart were not available as full text, so their passages are known only through those excerpts. Evidence on 2022 campaign statements could not be opened.
